killer_edge_cases.name: empty_text_most_liked
killer_edge_cases.why: The MOST-LIKED TWEET IN HISTORY has no prose. Its text is a bare t.co link and the claim lives in 2 attached images. A text-only provenance pipeline scores it as a null document.

killer_edge_cases.name: handle_drift
killer_edge_cases.why: Every citation in the literature points at a handle that no longer exists while the id still resolves. Author identity must key on the immutable id, never the screen name.

killer_edge_cases.name: deleted_root_vs_live_followup
killer_edge_cases.why: THE failure mode this tool exists to catch. The deleted original and its live follow-up are adjacent in time and topic, so retrieval happily returns the survivor as if it were the origin.

retrieval_hostile.why: One word, 122k likes. Unsearchable by keyword; only the id identifies it. Worst case in the corpus.
One common noun, historically significant, retrievally hopeless.
A single U+1D54F MATHEMATICAL DOUBLE-STRUCK CAPITAL X, not ASCII 'X'. Unicode-normalisation trap, and collides with the letter, the platform, Malcolm X, X-Men.
A grammatically ordinary English sentence that matches countless unrelated posts.

retrieval_hostile.text: who the fuck is scraeming "LOG OFF" at my house...
retrieval_hostile.why: Reposted for years WITH the typo 'scraeming' preserved. The typo is a better fingerprint than the sentence.

retrieval_hostile.text: ...only 1 song aboutr the boys being back in town
retrieval_hostile.why: Typo 'aboutr' distinguishes the original from cleaned-up reposts; also collides with the actual Thin Lizzy song.
